Let the roots be \(x,y,z\in(0,1)\) with \(x+y+z=1\). Then
\[
7a-9b=7(xy+yz+zx)-9xyz.
\]

Using Lagrange multipliers for the constraint \(x+y+z=1\), the stationary equations are
\[
7(1-x)-9yz=\lambda,\quad
7(1-y)-9xz=\lambda,\quad
7(1-z)-9xy=\lambda.
\]
Subtracting pairs gives
\[
(y-x)(7-9z)=0,\quad (z-y)(7-9x)=0,\quad (z-x)(7-9y)=0.
\]
The only feasible interior solution is
\[
x=y=z=\frac13.
\]
Indeed, if two variables are equal but not all three, the equations force one of them to be \(7/9\), impossible since the sum is \(1\).

At \(x=y=z=\frac13\),
\[
a=3\cdot \frac19=\frac13,\qquad b=\frac1{27},
\]
so
\[
7a-9b=\frac73-\frac13=2.
\]

On the boundary, as one root tends to \(0\), the expression tends at most to \(7/4<2\). Thus the maximum value is
\[
\boxed{2}.
\]
